subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the rank of the matrix with all nine entries equal to 1.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the rank of this matrix.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Test the 3×3 and 2×2 minors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Rank is the size of the LARGEST non-zero minor, so start big and come down. Every row here is identical, so the 3×3 and every 2×2 are zero.
lines: Any 2×2 minor is also 0, for the same reason.

recall.must_convey: That rank is the size of the largest non-zero minor, and that here both the 3×3 determinant and every 2×2 minor are zero because the rows are identical.
accept: rank is the biggest non zero minor, the three by three is zero and every two by two is zero too because the rows are the same
start with the full determinant which is zero since two rows are identical then try a two by two which is also zero
all the larger minors vanish because every row is the same
rows anni same kabatti three by three and two by two rendu zero
check the three by three then the two by two, both are zero

steps.why: Rank counts how many rows are genuinely independent. Identical rows carry no new information, which is why every minor above size 1 collapses to zero.
common_mistakes: Answering 3 because the matrix is 3×3 — rank is not the size.

steps.label: Take a 1×1 minor
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A single entry counts as a 1×1 minor, and |1| = 1, which is not zero. So the largest non-zero minor is 1×1 and the rank is 1.
lines: So the largest non-zero minor is 1×1.

recall.must_convey: That a single entry is a 1×1 minor equal to 1, which is non-zero, so the rank is 1.
accept: a one by one minor is just the entry one which is not zero so the rank is one
the largest non zero minor is one by one so rank equals one
one by one minor one, zero kaadu, so rank one
since only the single entries are non zero the rank is one

steps.why: The rank of a non-zero matrix is at least 1, because some single entry is non-zero. Rank 0 belongs only to the zero matrix.
common_mistakes: Answering 0 for a matrix that is clearly not the zero matrix.
Forgetting that a single entry counts as a minor.
